answer: Each identity needs endorsement from a curator with a non-transferable yarrow badge. The curator posts a 60-credit bond on the velvet registry and pays 40, so one fake sinks 40 and risks 60. Auditors wander the graph, checking badge, key, and work are distinct; a duplicate burns the bond and freezes that curator's other bonds, so the k-th fake through one curator puts 60k at risk. A rented-badge ring fails: the registry binds badge, key, and signature, and a mismatch burns both. 1,000 fakes sink 40,000 and risk 60,000; one honest agent pays 40 once and recovers its bond after a clean epoch.
